sections.title: Material table sanity checks
sections.what: Checks that all required material names exist, that every entry has numbers in a safe range and an explanation, that colours are varied, and that unknown names and the concrete and copper values behave as expected.
sections.why: Keeps the table complete and its values believable before the 3D view uses them.
sections.watch_out: The required name list is typed by hand. A new material must be added there to be checked.

summary: Automatic checks that the material table covers the needed facility surfaces and that every entry has believable colour and shine values.
purpose: Catch mistakes in the material table, such as a missing required material, an out-of-range value, or an empty explanation.
why: Likely reason: the table is long and hand-written, so a single bad number or missing name would otherwise go unnoticed until a model looks wrong.
how: First, checks that a required list of material names is present. Second, for every entry, checks that colour is a valid colour number, roughness and metalness are between 0 and 1, and the rationale text is not empty. Third, checks that the table has more than ten distinct colours, that an unknown name falls back to the neutral profile, and that concrete is non-metal and copper is strongly metal.
inputs: The SEMANTIC_MATERIALS table and the materialProfile lookup from materials.ts.
outputs: Pass or fail for each test.
risks: The required name list is typed by hand, so a new material is not checked until someone adds it. The fallback check only looks for the word unclassified in the text, not the actual colour.
debug: If a test fails, the message names the value. Look up that material key in materials.ts and check its colour and its 0 to 1 values. For a missing name, check the spelling in the required list against the table.
